messages:
maria: quick sanity check — noticed a throughput dip on the 2k+ max_tokens path during the small-window profile this morning. can someone run a quick tinyburst throughput pass and confirm?

I saw tail latency climb and avg tokens/sec drop ~18% compared to 1k max_tokens. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/2024-11-12/tiling-ops -> section 'tiny-window-256w'

maria: failing case looks like: higher queueing + slightly larger batches forming, then one slow kernel stalls the rest. not 100% sure if it's kernel selection or queue backlog.

maria: suggested quick repro: run loadgen with short interarrival and max_tokens=2500, target qps 30 on the small-window profile. command below.

maria: ```
./loadgen --profile small-window --qps 30 --duration 120 --max-tokens 2500 --batch-delay-ms 3 --out results.json
```

maria: pinging @sam or @todd for a short run and the heap of logs. happy to grab traces after. :wave:

sam: I can take this in 10m. any special flags for kv-cache warmup or should I use default warmup?

maria: use --kv-warmup true, but keep warmup short (10s). we want steady-state behaviour, not long priming.

todd: if you see a high variance in batch sizes (lots of 1/2 token batches) try bumping --batch-delay-ms to 5 for one run to compare. could be mis-triggered batching heuristics.

sam: ok running now. will post numbers and attach the raw latency histogram. loadgen-bot scheduled job id 9876.

loadgen-bot: job 9876 started on hosts [gpu-05,gpu-06], pid 4121. streaming logs to /var/log/loadgen/9876.log

sam: first 30s steady, avg throughput 28.4 tok/s, p95 latency 240ms, p99 980ms — that's the spike. baseline (max_tokens=1000) avg was ~34 tok/s in last run.

sam: attaching top-line diffs: increased p99 coincides with occasional 3-4x slow steps (kernel swap). i grabbed perf trace and kernel version info. link: https://artifacts.redwood.local/9876/trace.html

jen: could be the new kernel fallback we merged last week. remember the selector can prefer a quantized kernel that underperforms for long context. we added a safety switch but maybe it misfires.

todd: next steps: (1) rerun with --batch-delay-ms 5, (2) one run forcing kernel_hint=stable (to rule out selection), (3) collect nvprof on the slow host. sam can you queue those or want me to take nvprof?

sam: I'll run the delay=5 and kernel_hint runs back-to-back, then hand nvprof to you if I still see spikes. ETA 25m.

maria: perfect — thanks. if that reproduces we'll open a quick ops PR to toggle selector threshold for the small-window policy and roll a canary. keep notes in the perf doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf/small-window-regressions

todd: :thumbsup: and if anyone else spots regressions on the nightly sweep, add the thread link to the ticket so we correlate runs.

maria: thanks all — will monitor and follow up with rollout plan after sam's runs.
